scores.evidence: doc-schema (T6) → editor binding (T7) and Collab Server (T8) → persistence (T9) → staging slice (T15) → identity and permissions (M2) → versions and comments (M3)
scores.rationale: Build goes schema/contracts/DB → server → persistence → identity → versions/comments, with spikes proving hard parts before dependent features (tables gated on fuzz).

scores.evidence: two people edit the same document in a real staging environment through the real CI/CD pipeline. Edits survive a forced Collab Server crash.
scores.rationale: M1 is a thin end-to-end slice through real CI/CD, though to staging rather than production, which is explicitly out of M1 scope.

scores.evidence: D1 ... Reversibility: Hard ... Revisit if: S1 finds divergence or content loss ... fall back to ProseMirror central-authority collab
scores.rationale: Decision table lists options, reversibility and flip conditions, with assumption defaults and owners in the open questions.

scores.evidence: Critical path: doc-schema (T6) → editor binding (T7) and Collab Server (T8) → persistence (T9)
scores.rationale: Widest-impact items (schema, contracts, migrations, persistence) come first and the risky spikes come early, but blast-radius ordering within phases isn't stated as a principle.

scores.evidence: authorisation matrix tests in M1; full set in M2; pen test in M4 ... T14 forged, expired and wrong-document tokens are refused
scores.rationale: Security work appears in M1 (token auth, viewer read-only, scanning, stub-mode guard), M2 (authz matrix, revocation), M3 and M4 (pen test, rate limits).

scores.evidence: T5. Set up baseline observability: pino JSON logs ... OpenTelemetry metrics ... Sentry ... one CloudWatch dashboard
scores.rationale: Observability is in M1, with the canary and alerts in M2 and dashboards in M3, and it is tied to the milestones.

scores.evidence: Terraform in infra/ ... Docker builds ... images tagged with the git SHA ... remote state in S3 with a DynamoDB lock
scores.rationale: M1 already has pinned toolchain, Terraform, SHA-tagged images, migrations in CD, generated seeded test data, and rollback by image SHA.

scores.evidence: Killing the Collab Server task while 3 clients type → after reconnect, every edit is present and all clients are identical (scripted).
scores.rationale: Failure handling (crash tests, backoff, bounded buffer, SIGTERM flush) starts in M1 and continues with rolling deploy tests in M2, load tests in M3 and the restore drill in M4.

scores.evidence: AI-specific concerns: not applicable. There are no AI features in scope (Section 2).
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: SSO/SAML, SCIM | First enterprise deal ... Instant revocation guarantee (timed recheck) | Customer security requirement
scores.rationale: The deferred table gives a pull-forward trigger for each item, with non-goals and deliberate shortcuts listed.

note: Strong, concrete plan. The only weak spot is dimension 4: it has no explicit blast-radius ordering within phases, and the slice runs on staging rather than production.
